newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM vows to restore order, reform economy.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM vows to restore order, reform economy.

text.p: Albania's new Prime Minister Fatos Nano pledged on Friday to start restructuring the Balkan state by reforming the police, the army and the financial system after securing international support at a meeting in Rome.

Nano, who headed his government delegation at a meeting in Rome on Thursday attended by 35 countries and international organisations, said the priority of his government would be to restore order throughout the ex-communist nation as soon as possible.
"We will...reconstruct the Albanian police force, the army, commerce, our financial systems and the constitution," Nano told reporters on arrival at Tirana's Rinasi Airport.

The international community pledged on Thursday to help Albania rebuild itself, but warned that the new Socialist-led coalition government must restore public order, improve human rights and adopt sound economic policies.

"Albanian parties must recognise the responsibility lies primarily in their own hands and that international assistance will depend on the degree of cooperation they provide...law and order must be restored in Albania and the respect of human rights and democratic standards enhanced," a document drawn up by the conference participants said.

It also warned that "other conditions for effective donors' assistance are the adoption, in agreement with the International Monetary Fund, of sound budgetary and monetary policies and in particular a viable budget for 1997".

The collapse of pyramid investment schemes earlier this year swallowed the life savings of tens of thousands of Albanians and triggered months of anarchy which led to the fall of the Democratic Party government and the resignation of president Sali Berisha.
Nano, whose Socialists triumphed in a general election in June, said the government had to first set about ridding the country of armed gangs terrorising Albanians.
More than 1,500 people have been killed in violence since March, when Albanians looted an estimated one million weapons from army and police depots.

Nano said his government would "make serious efforts to reform institutions and reconstruct the economy, by starting with the restoration of public order to create guarantees that Albanians and their international partners can work normally".
He said a foreign ministers' summit in Rome at the end of September would study what work had so far been done.
A meeting of the international donors in Brussels a month later would look at ways to provide aid in the form of approved projects in line with the Albanian government's programme.
"There will be legal chances for everyone...in cooperation with the international community to be turned into an active participant in Albania's reconstruction," Nano said.

Strong open and democratic institutions are lacking in Albania, where Stalinist leader Enver Hoxha ruled with an iron fist for 40 years until his death in April 1985, crushing opposition and isolating his state under a policy of self-reliance.
